01 / Learn the language

Think in pairs.

Choose a pair to see what changes.
Always compare one structure with another.

TOWARD THE HEAD

Superior

Higher, toward the head.

For example

The head is superior to the chest.

↕
TOWARD THE FEET

Inferior

Lower, toward the feet.

For example

The ankle is inferior to the knee.

Describe the person's body in anatomical position, even when their posture changes.

Try one question +

The elbow is ____ to the wrist.

Choose the term that follows the limb toward its attachment.

Choose an answer to see the explanation.

03 / See the division

Name what the plane separates.

The word “vertical” alone is not enough.
Look at the portions on either side.

RL
01

Sagittal

Right and left portions.

At the midline: midsagittal, or median.
AP
02

Frontal

Anterior and posterior portions.

Also called the coronal plane.
SI
03

Transverse

Superior and inferior portions.

Also called the axial plane.

These icons show conceptual portions, not anatomical body views.

04 / The Study Bench approach

Understand it.
Then practise it.

Study Bench begins with one small corner of anatomy: the language used to describe where things are.

The references, exercises, and illustrations in this collection were created specifically for this pilot. The terminology was checked against the sources below.

  1. 01

    Make the comparison explicit.

    Name both structures. “Medial” only makes sense when you know what you are comparing.

  2. 02

    Practise without the prompt.

    Read the reference, cover it, and write your answer. Then put your reasoning into words.

  3. 03

    Check the explanation.

    Use the answer key to understand a mistake and decide which comparison to revisit.

A few useful details

Before you print.

What level is this collection for?

Students beginning anatomy or revisiting its basic directional language. The focus is intentionally narrow: ten directional terms, body planes, and anatomical position.

How should I print the PDFs?

Use US Letter paper and 100% scale. The exercises leave room for handwritten answers. You can also keep the PDFs open and answer in a notebook.

Are the answer keys included?

Yes. The worksheet has an answer page, and the practice pack has two answer-key pages with short explanations.

Can I use these with my course notes?

Yes. Use your course requirements as the guide. This collection includes common synonyms, such as frontal/coronal and transverse/axial.
